title: Efficiency-Resolved Recovery Dynamics of an Free-Running InGaAs/InP Single Photon Avalanche Detector Operated in Gated Mode
authors: Bruno Santos Souza, Vitor Tavares, Filippo Ghiglieno, Celso Jorge Villas-Boas, Paulo Henrique Dias Ferreira
abstract: Detection efficiency in gated-mode single-photon avalanche detectors recovers gradually after each gate edge, limiting attainable count rates, yet quantitative recovery models exist only for free-running operation. We extract the gated recovery time constant of a free-running InGaAs/InP detector at 1550 nm by sweeping the gate frequency from 100 kHz to 1 MHz and globally fitting count rates across four dead times, requiring neither a pulsed laser nor a time-to-digital converter. The recovery time decreases linearly with detection efficiency, from 301 to 161 ns between 10 % and 25 %, at 9.3 ns per percentage point. We further resolve a periodic count-rate modulation consistent with bias-dependent capacitive gate feedthrough.
summary: This work characterizes the recovery dynamics of gated SPADs by sweeping the gate frequency, revealing that the recovery time constant systematically decreases as detection efficiency increases. The authors developed a sophisticated model that successfully accounts for both the exponential recharge process and parasitic capacitive modulations in the count rate. This provides crucial, quantitative data for optimizing SPAD performance in quantum key distribution systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of characterizing the recovery dynamics of Single Photon Avalanche Detectors (SPADs) when operated in a gated mode, as this recovery process limits the achievable count rates in practical quantum communication systems.
main_result: The recovery time constant ($	au_{rec}$) was found to decrease linearly with increasing detection efficiency ($\eta$), a dependence that contrasts with previous assumptions for free-running detectors. The analysis also resolved a periodic modulation in the count rate attributed to capacitive gate feedthrough.
method: A novel frequency-sweep method using continuous-wave illumination was employed to globally fit count rates across multiple dead times, avoiding the need for high-speed pulsed lasers or time-to-digital converters.
model_or_system: The physical system is an InGaAs/InP SPAD operated in a gated mode. The analysis uses an exponential recovery model ($\eta(t)$) and incorporates a 'Full Model' that accounts for discrete re-arming and capacitive ripple effects beyond simple dead-time limitations.
key_observables: Count rate $C(f)$ as a function of gate frequency $f$, and the recovery time constant $	au_{rec}$ as a function of detection efficiency $\eta$.
important_parameters: Recovery time constant ($	au_{rec}$), Detection Efficiency ($\eta$), Gate Frequency ($f$), and modulation parameters ($a, f_0, \phi$).
main_assumptions: The detection efficiency recovers exponentially toward a steady-state value ($\eta_0$), and the analysis relies on fitting count rates across multiple dead times using a global least-squares approach.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the exponential recovery profile, the dependence of $	au_{rec}$ on $\eta$, and the count rate modulation curves compared between baseline and full models.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of gated recovery limits, develops and compares theoretical models (Baseline vs. Full Model) incorporating recharge dynamics and ripple effects, presents the frequency-sweep measurement methodology, and concludes with quantitative results on $	au_{rec}(\eta)$ and modulation analysis.
why_interesting: While the core physics is semiconductor device characterization, the rigorous application of time-domain modeling (exponential recovery) and advanced statistical fitting (AIC/BIC model selection) to extract fundamental physical constants ($	au_{rec}$) from complex, rate-limited measurements is relevant to open quantum systems modeling.

Vertical lines mark three gate durations tA < tB < tC, equivalently three gate frequencies fA > fB > fC through t = W = D/f: at short gate duration (tA) neither curve has saturated, while at long gate duration (tC) both approach their respective plateaus.
